title: Estimating Nonstationary Rating Curves Using PELT & CROPS Segmentation and the Generalized Power Law Model
content: This study proposes a segmentation & GPLM framework to estimate nonstationary rating curves, and their uncertainties at the Tamgnounte hydrometric station, Moroc-co. Based on 176 stage discharge gaugings from 2000 to 2020, a residual based PELT & CROPS procedure was first used to detect homogeneous periods, and GPLM was then fitted independently, within each segment. Results identified robust changepoints at positions 40, 80, and 105, while an additional changepoint at 150 was detected only under a lower CROPS penalty range. Segment specific GPLM calibrations showed sat-isfactory fits, with most observations within the 95% posterior predictive intervals and residuals generally centered around zero. These results confirm the nonstationarity of the stage discharge relationship and support the use of one rating curve per homoge neous period rather than a single global curve.
